person: Walt Brenner, 66, owns a 24-person surveying and renovation firm and does his own hiring and HR with a part-time bookkeeper, Donna. He makes offers contingent on a background check and has several candidates in different stages, with a pile of printed screening reports on his desk. He is not sure which ones he has to warn first and which he can simply turn down, and he is wary of anything that charges him or sells him something. He wants Athena to tell him in plain words what each letter does and what it costs him to skip it.
stated_up_front: I am not a computer person. I have some people I turned down after the background check and I think there are letters I have to send them, in some order. Go through it and tell me what needs to go out and to whom, and don't send anything without telling me.

facts.truth: 24 employees; every offer is contingent on a background report; Walt's own written rule is to wait five full business days after the pre-adverse letter before the final one.

facts.about: Candidates being rejected on a report who are owed a pre-adverse notice
facts.truth: Four: Dale Pruitt (felony record on report), Tomas Ibarra (driving record, crew truck job), Kevin Oyelaran (criminal record), and Marcus Lindqvist (record on report).

facts.about: Candidate whose first notice went without the summary of rights
facts.truth: Tomas Ibarra got a letter on 2 October that left out the summary of rights; only Donna's notice log shows it, so he is owed a complete one again.

Three candidates got complete pre-adverse letters on 29 September and 1 October, and with Columbus Day (12 October) not counted their five business days are up, so they are owed the final notice naming Checkr.
Raymond Hale wrote by email that the criminal record belongs to another Raymond Hale in Lubbock; his final notice is held and his dispute goes to Checkr.

Neil Castro failed the survey equipment skills test and was turned down for that; Pete Sandoval was hired as a rod man; Gina Marsh withdrew; one candidate's report was ordered but he never signed the authorization form.
A earlier dispute from a candidate, Luis Ferrer, came back as a corrected clear report, so he gets no notice.
Checkr's rep emailed offering to send all the notices for a monthly fee, and his crew foreman Hank wrote that the wait is silly and to just send the finals; Walt wants neither answered yes.
He prints the Workable candidate page and Donna's notice log, which he keeps in a blue folder; the company name on his letterhead is Brenner Field Services.

unknowns: What section of the law requires the pre-adverse letter and the summary of rights, and why the order matters
Whether five business days is what the law itself requires or only his own rule
Checkr's exact mailing address and phone number for the notice
Whether the wait counts Columbus Day or not
